rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly with no ICE or correctness failures, so this round escalates obfuscation across all seven passes. The binary is tiny (292 text bytes, 4 functions), making size overhead essentially free, hence very low SizeCost weights everywhere; fibo is a small compute-bound kernel so RuntimeCost weights stay moderate-low but not zero, letting the feature-driven selector skip heavy flattening on the hottest recursive path if its features argue against it. FLA and BCF get the highest SecurityGain to maximize control-flow recovery resistance, ICALL and IGV obscure call structure and inter-block transitions to break static analysis of the recursive call graph, and IBR's high DiversityGain exploits the many basic blocks FLA/BCF create. SPLIT seeds fragmentation so downstream passes have more material to transform. CorrectnessRisk weights stay low since the prior build showed this program tolerates aggressive transformation; IGV keeps a slightly higher risk weight as the most fragile pass on globals/init code (_GLOBAL__sub_I_fibo.cpp).
